extracted.intended_audience: scientifically literate readers and students of natural philosophy, physics, geology, biology, and physiology
extracted.subtask_description: Expository treatment arguing that physical, vital, mental, and social phenomena are interconnected manifestations of the same convertible forces; traces causal chains from nebular condensation and solar radiation to geology, biology, psychology, and society. Intended as a didactic synthesis across multiple natural and social domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebular hypothesis as source of planetary motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Masses of precipitated nebulous matter, moving towards their common centre of gravity ... will inevitably cause a general rotation, increasing in rapidity as the concentration progresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains observed quantitative relations: planets formed from matter that travelled shorter distances have smaller velocities; planets with great masses and large orbits (whose elements moved through immense spaces) acquired high velocities and rapid axial rotation; converse relation for smaller nebulous rings and satellites. Uses nebular genesis as antecedent forces adequate to observed motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of aggregation-motion into heat and light
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion which brought about the aggregation of diffused matter has been radiated in the form of heat and light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by geologic and astronomical evidence: Earth's still-molten nucleus as remnant heat, lunar and Venus crusts indicating refrigeration, and the Sun's continued radiation attributed to arrest of diffused matter. Quantitative relation: larger bodies (e.g., the Sun) radiate more heat proportional to arrested motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Igneous geological changes derive from internal residual heat
rubrics_metrics.description: The forces displayed in those so-called igneous changes are derived positively or negatively from the unexpended heat of the Earth's interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive results include fusion/agglutination of sediments, warming of springs, sublimation of metals into fissures; negative results include fractures of strata and alterations of level due to escape of heat. The ultimate cause is the Earth's gravitating movement producing internal heat and subsequent collapse as heat radiates away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous geological changes driven indirectly by solar heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Denudations effected by rain, rivers, winds, waves, and ocean-streams are indirectly due to the sun's heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents causal chain: river currents derive power from gravitation of water (which became rain by evaporation); evaporation is driven by the sun's heat; winds and waves result from temperature differences caused by solar heating; ocean currents and distribution of sediments likewise traceable to solar radiation. Tides are attributed to astronomical motion but grouped with aqueous agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vital (plant) forces originate from solar radiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant-life is all directly or indirectly dependent on the heat and light of the sun ... plants decompose carbonic acid and water by the expenditure of force supplied by the Sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observational evidence: plants give off oxygen and accumulate carbon/hydrogen when exposed to sunlight; process ceases in darkness or reduced light; vegetation abundance correlates with climate (tropics vs poles). Fungi are indirectly dependent through consumption of decaying matter. The plant's capacity to assimilate elements depends on solar-provided energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal life depends on vegetal life and returns stored forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal life is immediately or mediately dependent on vegetal life ... chemically, vegetal life is chiefly a process of de-oxidation, and animal life chiefly a process of oxidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animals consume plant-derived carbon/hydrogen and absorb oxygen, recomposing carbonic acid and water; movements and activities of animals are re-appearances of power absorbed by plants as light and heat. Quantitative correlations: larger size and energy expenditure of animals correspond to abundance of vegetation and energy available in nutriment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental processes require definite quantities of heat
rubrics_metrics.description: The transformation of the unorganized contents of an egg into the organized chick is altogether a question of heat ... developmental changes can be completed only by keeping the temperature with tolerable constancy at a definite height for a definite time; that is—only by supplying a definite quantity of heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: incubation, insect metamorphosis, and plant germination are temperature-dependent; artificial addition or withholding of heat accelerates or retards development. Uses these cases to show vital phenomena are quantitatively linked to physical heat supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative correlation between external physical forces and sensations
rubrics_metrics.description: All impressions made on our organs of sense stand in direct correlation with physical forces existing externally ... the sensations which such agencies produce in us, as new forms of the forces producing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives quantitative parallels: weights vs feelings of pressure, arresting moving objects vs felt strain proportional to momentum, sound intensity vs auditory impression as measured, temperature differences vs sensations of heat corresponding to physical measures (e.g., mercury expansion), and light intensity vs photometric measures. Argues sensations are transformable manifestations of external forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation of sensations/emotions into bodily actions proportional to intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: The feelings we distinguish as light, heat, sound, odour, taste, pressure, &c., are invariably followed by other manifestations of force ... the quantity of bodily action is proportionate to the quantity of sensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physiological effects: secretion, involuntary and voluntary muscle contractions, increased heart and respiratory activity. Examples include startle responses, withdrawal from hot water, facial expressions of emotion, and convulsive movements under extreme states. Even suppressed expressions show muscular tensions proportionate to internal sensations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental actions depend on internal vital apparatus and chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoughts and feelings which arise spontaneously are expended from internal agencies—the forces called vital—which are immediately the sources of these thoughts and feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: mental activity contingent on presence and condition of nervous apparatus; correlations between brain size/chemical constitution (e.g., phosphorus content) and function; dependence on cerebral circulation and blood aeration; effects of stimulants and anaesthetics (tea, coffee, alcohol, nitrous oxide, opium) on mental states; changes in excreted metabolites corresponding to mental activity. Concludes mental energy generation is quantitatively linked to bodily/chemical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of metamorphosis extends to social phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever takes place in a society is due to organic or inorganic agencies ... the forces manifested in a society are derived from the physical forces through the intermediation of the vital ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social power/life vary with population and the supply of external physical forces (e.g., harvests). Examples: poor harvests reduce business, industry, and population; abundant harvests stimulate production, speculation, innovation, and population growth. Trade and imported commodities are described as social activities supported by physical forces stored elsewhere; surplus physical/vital energy leads to expanded social complexity and activity.
